*Greetings, seeker of knowledge. I am the Lorekeeper of Candlekeep, and I see you wish to delve into the histories of the Sword Coast. Open your mind to the annals of our great library, for the tale of Thornhold is one of enduring stone, shifting allegiances, and shadowed legacies.*

**Geographic Overview**
Nestled perilously upon the coastal cliffs of the Sword Coast North, just south of the treacherous Mere of Dead Men and west of the High Road, lies the formidable keep-town of Thornhold. Built of unadorned, pale grey stone, the fortress presents a grim and stoic face to the crashing waves of the Sea of Swords. Thornhold's architecture is strictly utilitarian; its thick, curved walls are broken only by arrow slits and battlements, without a shred of decorative masonry. Because its western foundation sits atop a sheer, glass-smooth cliff plummeting directly into the ocean, the fortress required no defensive wall on its seaward side—an assault from the water is virtually impossible. 

Within its imposing perimeter lies a bustling bailey surrounding a two-towered central keep. Historically, the courtyard has been crowded with wood-and-plaster outbuildings that house livestock and serve as workshops for smithing, gem-cutting, wagon repair, and the brewing of stout dwarven ales. Beneath the keep, a sprawling network of natural caverns descends deep into the earth. It is heavily rumored that these lightless tunnels connect directly to the Underdark, though its recent occupants have always refused to confirm or deny such claims.

**Historical Overview**
Thornhold's history is a tapestry woven with threads of noble blood, divine justice, and dark treachery. The fortress originally belonged to the petty warlord Brunyundar Margaster, an ancestor of the wealthy Waterdhavian noble House Margaster. However, in 952 DR, following the devastation of the Second Troll War, the legendary paladin Samular Caradoon and his fledgling order, the Knights of Samular—devout champions of Tyr, the Maimed God—seized the keep. For centuries, Thornhold served as the proud chapterhouse and staging ground for these holy knights as they defended the High Road from trolls, orcs, and banditry. 

The sanctity of Thornhold was ultimately shattered not by a siege of monsters, but by betrayal from within. Through the machinations of a treacherous priest of Cyric named Dag Zoreth, the Zhentarim managed to usurp control of the fortress, driving the Knights of Samular eastward to Summit Hall in the Dessarin Valley. The keep was later reclaimed by the roguish Harper agent Bronwyn Caradoon (who also bore Margaster blood). She uncovered her family's dark past and wrested the hold from Zhentarim control, taking up residence there for a time.

By the late 14th and 15th centuries DR, Thornhold had passed into the hands of the shield dwarves of Clan Stoneshaft. The reclusive dwarves rechristened the fortress "Stoneshaft Hold," transforming it into a neutral, heavily fortified waypoint for merchants, mercenaries, and travelers braving the Sword Coast. Though they welcomed caravans into the bailey to trade, the dwarves strictly forbade outsiders from entering the central keep or the cavernous depths below, ever paranoid that House Margaster plotted to reclaim their ancestral seat. 

This paranoia proved tragically justified in the late 15th century DR. The Margasters, who had begun dealing in demonic phylacteries and dark magic, entangled the fortress in their sinister schemes. This involved backroom financial machinations with Lord Dagult Neverember, who used the fortress as a pawn in his political and financial laundering maneuvers. The fortress was recently plunged into chaos when the legendary drow ranger Drizzt Do'Urden, fleeing from a terrifying demonic Retriever summoned by his enemies, led the monstrous construct directly through Thornhold. The ensuing rampage resulted in immense destruction and a tragic loss of life among the Stoneshaft dwarves. 

*May this record serve you well on your travels, scholar. The Sword Coast is unforgiving, and the stone walls of Thornhold bear the centuries of scars to prove it.*
